newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Q4 trading conditions up - survey.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Q4 trading conditions up - survey.

text.p: Business trading conditions in Australia improved slightly in the December quarter, according to a National Australia Bank (NAB) survey released on Monday.
The modest improvement met the previous NAB Quarterly Business Survey's finding that businesses expected a slight upturn in trading conditions in the three months to December.
However, the December survey said business conditions remained relatively subdued despite the small upturn and after another small contraction in the previous quarter.

The December quarter found profitability was also improved slightly but was still short of expectations reported in the previous survey. It found employment was largely unchanged for the fifth consecutive quarter.
Forward orders rose slightly in the December quarter after large falls since early 1995 and stocks increased further contrary to expectations of a fall.
"Price pressures eased further from the already low levels reported in the September quarter, and are anticipated to remain subdued in the near term," the survey said.
The bank said businesses surveyed reported price increases of 0.2 percent in the December quarter, compared with 0.3 percent in the previous quarter.

"Tough trading conditions in manufacturing and retailing contribudted importantly to this result - with price increases in those sectors 0.08 and 0.15 percent, respectively," NAB chief economist Alan Oster said in a commentary.

The survey found business conditions were expected to improve slightly in the March quarter, but said this may be a little optimistic given current activity levels, continued destocking intentions and poor levels of forward orders.

"Looking further ahead, respondents continue to anticipate a pickup in business conditions over the next twelve months - mainly in terms of output and profitability, rather than employment," Oster said.

He said inflationary expectations had improved further with 92 percent of respondents expecting inflation to remain below 4 percent over the remainder of the decade. This compared to 89 percent of respondents in the September quarter.
The survey also posed a number of questions on the potential of the government's new industrial relations legislation to change employment intentions.
Oster said 70 percent of respondents expected no short-term (next 6 months) impact on their employment intentions from the new legislation.
More positive responses were recorded for the medium term (over the next 18 to 24 months), he said.
NAB raised its growth forecast to 2.75 percent for 1996/97 from 2.4 percent in the previous forecast.
